traditionalDress.men: Kurta-pajama paired with a turban (pagri); the Patiala shahi style of turban, associated with the former royal court of Patiala, is especially well known, along with the wide-legged Patiala salwar-style trousers.
traditionalDress.women: The salwar kameez, often paired with a phulkari (embroidered) dupatta; the Patiala suit — featuring heavily pleated, voluminous trousers — is a well-known regional variation.

festivals.name: Baisakhi
festivals.description: A harvest festival and Punjabi New Year that also marks the founding of the Khalsa in Sikh tradition, celebrated with fairs, Bhangra and Giddha performances, and gurdwara visits.

festivals.name: Lohri
festivals.description: A winter bonfire festival marking the end of the coldest days, celebrated with folk songs, dancing, and offerings of sesame seeds, jaggery, and popcorn thrown into the fire.

festivals.name: Hola Mohalla
festivals.description: A Sikh festival held the day after Holi at Anandpur Sahib, featuring displays of martial arts, mock battles, and Gatka (traditional sword-fighting).

music: Folk music played on dhol, tumbi, and chimta
cuisine: Sarson da Saag with Makki di Roti
folklore: Heer Ranjha, immortalized in the 18th-century poet Waris Shah's telling, is Punjab's best-known tragic love legend: a herdsman named Ranjha and a wealthy family's daughter, Heer, fall in love but are separated by family opposition, and the story ends in their deaths — it is often read as an allegory for the soul's longing for the divine.
